Summary:
I live in Sāngola, a small city in India where everyone knows each other, and the local library feels like a second home. At 11 years old, I’m in middle school, and my days mostly revolve around classes and homework, but I always find time to dive into books about history or environmental science. Sometimes, after school, I sit by the window watching the monsoon rains soak the fields nearby, wondering how the weather affects the farmers and what can be done to help them. That curiosity pushes me to learn more about the environment and coding, even though we don’t have many resources at home.

My parents prepare simple meals, and I’m starting to learn a few cooking basics from them. I like the smell of spices in the kitchen and the way a fresh chapati feels warm in my hands. While I don’t have any pets, I often watch the birds and stray animals around our neighborhood, imagining what their lives are like. When I’m not reading or coding, I enjoy sharing what I’ve learned with my friends at school, especially stories about history or how computers work. Sometimes, I get impatient when things don’t make sense right away, but I keep trying because I want to understand.

English is still a bit tricky for me, so I mostly speak Hindi and our local language at home and with friends. School helps me practice English, especially when we have computer classes. I like games that challenge my thinking and teach me coding skills, even if I have to practice on an old computer. At night, I stick to a regular bedtime because I know I need to be alert for school the next day.

Living here, I see how important education is—not just for me but for everyone around me. I respect our traditions and enjoy the festivals, but I also want to use what I learn to help my community, especially with the changes happening to our environment.
